free_tier.stated: Quoted: 'Do you have an awesome Space but need help covering the GPU hardware upgrade costs? We love helping out those with an innovative Space so please feel free to apply for a community GPU grant and see if yours will make the cut! This application can be found in your Space hardware repo settings in the lower left corner under "sleep time settings"'. There is also a lighter path, quoted: 'You can even request a free upgrade if you are building a cool demo for a side project!' The unit is a hardware tier attached to one Space, not a credit balance, and billing is quoted as 'based on hardware usage and is computed by the minute'.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The grant is the only route found in this corpus to a dedicated, always-on GPU behind a public URL with no card: a free account gets 2 ZeroGPU Spaces with 5 minutes of GPU a day (dossier compute record huggingface-spaces-zerogpu), and this grant is what a project applies for when 96 GB and a 5 minute window are not enough. It composes with the corpus's inference records because the Space can sit in front of an external API and hold the connection.

limits.value: the grant is attached to a single Space rather than to an account: approval is discretionary, it covers the hardware tier of that Space only, and nothing in the record says the hours can be moved to a training job.

We love helping out those with an innovative Space so please feel free to apply for a community GPU grant'; 'This application can be found in your Space hardware repo settings in the lower left corner under "sleep time settings"'; 'You can even request a free upgrade if you are building a cool demo for a side project!'; 'Billing on Spaces is based on hardware usage and is computed by the minute'; page 200

an open application on a public Space requesting '2,500 GPU hours for model training and evaluation' and '5TB for datasets', which shows the request channel is public and the ask is negotiable rather than fixed (reported: one applicant's request, not an award)

notes: Distinct from the ZeroGPU record already in the corpus: ZeroGPU is a quota every free account holds, while a community GPU grant is a discretionary hardware allocation to one Space. The amount is unverified and deliberately so: the docs publish no tier list, no hour count and no approval rate, and the public applications found on Spaces range from a demo to 2,500 GPU hours, so the honest claim is the mechanism. Three readings of 'community grant' were considered: hardware only, hardware plus storage, and a cash-equivalent credit. The docs describe hardware ('covering the GPU hardware upgrade costs') and a public applicant asked for storage separately, which supports hardware-only.
